evidence.note: Lopes and Cornelli treat Letter III within a modern framework that rejects all canonical letters except VII and VIII as Platonic.
The contemporary review of Morrow's Studies reports that Morrow accepted Letter III as authentic.
Helfer (2023) argues for the literary unity and Platonic authorial design of the Letters as a whole.

rationale: Letter III has long attracted materially stronger defenses than the clearest spurious letters. Morrow accepted it, whereas Bury and recent work by Lopes and Cornelli reject it; Helfer's 2023 monograph again treats the collection as a unified Platonic composition. The evidence therefore reflects a genuine authorship dispute rather than a stable consensus, so B is more faithful than either A or C.
